landing.mattersIntro: Vaccinating pets protects them — and the people around them. In the World Health Organization's words:

matters.preventable: Rabies is a vaccine-preventable, zoonotic, viral disease affecting the central nervous system.
matters.dogs: Dog bites and scratches cause 99% of the human rabies cases and can be prevented through dog vaccination and bite prevention.
matters.vaccinating: Vaccinating dogs, including puppies, through mass dog vaccination programs is the most cost-effective strategy for preventing rabies in people because it stops the transmission at its source.

landing.closing: Takes about two minutes with the demo accounts.

help.title: Bitten or scratched by an animal?
help.intro: Act now. Rabies can be prevented with prompt care after an exposure.
help.stepWashBody: Wash the bite or scratch with soap and running water for at least 15 minutes.
help.stepCareBody: Go to a hospital or health centre as soon as you can, even if the wound looks small. A health worker will decide what care you need, which may include vaccination.
help.whyBody: According to the World Health Organization, once rabies symptoms appear the disease is virtually always fatal. Care after an exposure prevents that.
help.call112: National emergency number in India. It connects to police, fire and health emergency services.
help.call15400: National Rabies Helpline. The programme lists it as serving five states/UTs: Andhra Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Assam, Puducherry and Delhi. Check whether it covers your area.
help.notDoBody: PawGuard cannot tell you whether an animal has rabies, and you never need to photograph or approach the animal to get help. Your own care does not depend on finding the animal.
help.reviewNotice: Starter guidance. It follows the WHO rabies fact sheet but has not yet been reviewed by a qualified local health professional for your area.

learn.title: Learn
learn.body: Short, reviewed lessons about living safely alongside community animals are planned for a later release. Until then, the guidance for what to do after a bite is available now.
learn.helpLink: What to do after a bite

findCare.meanwhileBody: Go to the nearest government hospital or primary health centre, or call 112 in an emergency.
findCare.helpLink: What to do after a bite

about.title: About PawGuard 360
about.body1: PawGuard 360 is a software prototype for community rabies prevention programmes. It is being built to keep animal vaccination records trustworthy, show uncertainty honestly, and help teams coordinate field work.
about.body2: It is not a clinically validated service, it is not endorsed by any government programme, and it has not yet been piloted with a partner organisation.
about.statusBody: Prevention record-keeping for trained teams, in development. Other modules are listed only when they work.

imports.title: Data imports
imports.intro: Bring in records from a partner's spreadsheet. Every file is checked first; nothing is created until you apply it.
imports.uploadIntro: Upload a UTF-8 CSV file (up to 2 MB). You will see a row-by-row report before anything changes.

types.vaccinations_csv: Vaccination records (arrive as submitted for review)

columns.animals_csv: Columns: source_row_id (required), nickname, species, sex, sterilisation_status, age_band, ownership_category, area_code, last_seen_date, latitude, longitude, coat_description, identifying_marks.
columns.vaccinations_csv: Columns: source_row_id and animal_reference (required), administered_on, date_precision, product_name, lot_number, administered_by_name, registration.

imports.sourceHint: For example: "Partner shelter export, September". Kept with every imported record.
imports.dateFormat: Date format used in the file
imports.fileHint: Values are trimmed and mapped to PawGuard's vocabulary; unclear values are flagged, never guessed.
imports.labelRequired: Say where the file is from.
imports.failed: The file could not be checked.
imports.notAppliedBody: Review the rows below. Rejected rows and rows imported before are never applied. Possible matches with existing records are only hints — a reviewer decides about merges.
imports.apply: Apply {count, plural, one {# row} other {# rows}}
imports.applyConfirm: Create records from {count, plural, one {# row} other {# rows}}?
imports.applyExplain: Records are created in one step and marked with this import. Animal profiles start as provisional; vaccination records arrive as "submitted for review".
imports.rollbackExplain: Records that nobody has used since the import are archived (kept for the history, hidden from searches). If any were used, roll back is refused.

identity.previewBody: This demo organisation can try photo-based suggestions from a research model. It has only been tested on a research set of dog face photos, not on community dogs in the field. It is not offered for real records. Always compare the photos and details yourself.
identity.step1: 1. Add a photo and choose the animal in it
identity.chooseSubjectFirst: Choose which animal in the photo you mean before searching.
identity.tookTooLong: The search is taking longer than expected. Search the registry instead, or try again later.
identity.noneNew: None of these — register a new animal
identity.notSureSaved: Saved as "not sure". Nothing was linked. You can search the registry or ask a colleague.
identity.confirmTitle: Record this photo as a sighting of {ref}?
identity.confirmBody: Only confirm if the photos and details clearly show the same animal. The sighting is saved with today's date; you can add details from the profile.
identity.completedBody: These are animals whose photos look similar. They are suggestions, not identifications — similar-looking dogs are common. If none is clearly the same animal, choose "None of these" or "Not sure".
identity.noCandidateTitle: No confident match — check manually or register a new dog
identity.noCandidateBody: None of the {n} animals with photos on record reached the confidence threshold, so no suggestion is shown. This does not prove the dog is new: search the registry by description, or register it if you are sure.
identity.staleBody: Some recent photos have not been added to the comparison yet, so a matching animal could be missing. Search the registry as well.
identity.qualityTitle: The chosen area is too small to compare
identity.qualityBody: Choose the animal in a closer or clearer photo, or search the registry by description.
identity.failedTitle: Photo comparison didn't work this time
identity.failedBody: Search the registry by reference, nickname or description, or register the animal. Nothing was linked.
identity.researchOnly: A research model exists, but it has not passed validation on field photos, so it is not offered for real records.

campaigns.title: Campaign planning
campaigns.intro: Plan field days: which team visits which areas, in what order, within shifts, access times and doses.
campaigns.name: Name
campaigns.needNameAndAreas: Give the campaign a name and choose at least one area.
campaigns.plannerIntro: Set what you know about each area, choose the teams, then make a plan. A plan is a proposal: nothing is sent to teams until you approve and publish it.
campaigns.inputsIntro: Enter your own estimate, or use the suggestion: the latest street count for the area, otherwise the number of registered animals there.
campaigns.speedHint: Used for a straight-line travel estimate; no road routing is configured.
campaigns.noTeams: No teams yet. Add teams before planning.
campaigns.overridesHint: Keep an area with one team, or leave it out. These are respected in every new version.
campaigns.failedTitle: The plan could not be made
campaigns.failedBody: Check the inputs and try again. Teams can still be assigned tasks by hand.
campaigns.proposalBody: Check it with the teams. Times are estimates and animal numbers are planning estimates; nothing is sent until you approve and publish.

reason.no_location: The area has no map location, so travel cannot be estimated.
reason.no_animals_estimated: No animals are expected there yet (add a count or an estimate).
reason.pinned_team_not_in_plan: It is kept for a team that is not in this plan.
reason.longer_than_any_shift: The work there takes longer than any team's shift — split the area or plan more days.
reason.needs_more_doses_than_any_team: It needs more doses than any team carries.
reason.cannot_fit_in_access_window_and_shift: Its access times do not fit any team's shift.
reason.not_enough_time_or_doses_left: Teams' time or doses ran out on higher-priority or closer areas.

campaigns.approveBody: Approval records that you checked it. It does not send anything to teams yet.
campaigns.publishTitle: Create {n, plural, one {# task} other {# tasks}} for the teams?
campaigns.publishBody: Each planned stop becomes a task assigned to its team, with the planned times. Tasks from earlier versions stay as they are.
campaigns.publishedTasks: {n, plural, one {# task was} other {# tasks were}} created.
campaigns.suggestedRegistry: Suggested {n}: registered animals with this home area
campaigns.estimatesBody: A street count is what one person saw on one day: it can miss animals and count some twice. Registry numbers include only registered animals. Only the latest count is used — counts are never added up. These numbers schedule time and doses; they are not population sizes or vaccination coverage.

welcome.title: Welcome to the PawGuard 360 demo
welcome.intro: PawGuard helps pet owners keep vaccination records and get reminders before each due date, with every record verified by the clinic's vet. It also supports community rabies programmes.
welcome.fictionalBody: This demo uses fictional accounts, pets and clinics. You sign in with one click on the next page — no password to type. Please don't upload photos of people or private places.
welcome.howTitle: Community dog programmes: try it in four steps (about 3 minutes)

one.title: Sign in as Priya (field volunteer)
one.body: Click “Let's start”, then “Sign in as Priya”.

two.title: Find a dog from a photo
two.body: Open “Add photo”, choose the sample dog photo below, pick “Dog 1”, then “Look for possible matches”. Compare the photos, then choose “This is the same animal” → “Yes, same animal”.

three.title: Submit vaccination evidence
three.body: On the animal's page choose “Record vaccination evidence”: yesterday's date, product “DEMO Rabies Vaccine A (fictional)”, lot “DEMO-A-001”, any name, and the sample certificate. Then “Submit for review”.

four.title: Verify as the vet
four.body: Sign out, choose “Sign in as Dr Arun”, open “Review”, select the record and “Verify”. Sign in as Priya again: the animal now shows its last verified vaccination record.

welcome.filesIntro: Download these to your device to use in the steps above.
welcome.sampleDogCredit: Photo: Flickr 3572256424 via the COCO 2017 dataset, CC BY 2.0.
welcome.sampleCertificate: Sample vaccination certificate (for the evidence step)
welcome.sampleCertificateNote: A made-up certificate image created for this demo.

limits.matching: Photo matching is a research preview: tested only on a set of pet-dog face photos, not on community dogs, and it does not pass our own accuracy bar. Suggestions are never automatic — a person decides.
limits.offline: Offline mode covers tasks and sightings only; photos and vaccination evidence need a connection.
limits.language: Tamil and Hindi are partial drafts; some screens appear in English.
limits.reset: Demo data may be reset at any time.
limits.reminders: Reminders appear in the app. Email, browser notifications and WhatsApp are opt-in; in the demo they go only to the team's test inbox and test WhatsApp number. Seeded due dates are fictional; the app only reminds and never decides treatment.

welcome.petHowTitle: Pet vaccination reminders: try it in five steps (about 2 minutes)

one.title: Sign in as Neha (pet owner)
one.body: Click “Let's start”, then “Sign in as Neha”. Three demo pets: Bruno is up to date, Misty is due soon, Coco is overdue.

two.title: Act on a reminder
two.body: Open “Reminders”. Open “Notification preview” to see the message text, or “Add to calendar”. On Coco's reminder choose “Mark as done”, add the sample certificate below and save.

three.title: Verify as the clinic vet
three.body: Sign out, choose “Sign in as Dr Kiran”, open “Clinic”. Under “Awaiting verification” choose “Review” for Coco, then “Verify” with a next due date.

four.title: Move the demo date
four.body: On the clinic dashboard choose “+7 days”: Misty moves to “Due this week”. Choose “Back to the real date” when done.

five.title: Show the QR card
five.body: Sign in as Neha again: Coco is up to date. Open Coco → “Vaccination card (QR)” to see the QR code, the public card and the PDF.

modelEvidence.title: Model evidence: photo matching
modelEvidence.intro: What we measured about the photo-matching research preview, on a public dataset, with the model frozen.
modelEvidence.caveatLine: Evaluated on DogFaceNet pet face photos; not yet validated on street dogs.
modelEvidence.caveatBody: DogFaceNet is a public set of close-up face photos of pet dogs. Our field photos are full-body photos of community dogs, taken outdoors in very different conditions, so these numbers do not tell us how well matching works in the field.
modelEvidence.status: Offered only in demo organisations, always with a person deciding. Our release bar is not met, so real organisations cannot use it.
modelEvidence.what: {known} known dogs had {gallery} photos on record (2 each); {knownQ} other photos of them were searched. {unknown} more dogs were never put on record; their {unknownQ} photos should get no confident match. None of these dogs were used to build the model, and the settings were chosen beforehand on {valDogs} separate validation dogs.
modelEvidence.threshold: Confidence threshold {tau} (similarity to the average of a dog's photos on record), chosen on the validation dogs to keep false matches for unknown dogs at or below 5 %.
modelEvidence.closedTitle: Is the right dog ranked first? (known dogs only)
modelEvidence.closedNote: {q} searches for {d} known dogs. Brackets: 95 % confidence interval (bootstrap over dogs, 1,000 resamples).

open.fpir: Unknown dog wrongly given a confident match

modelEvidence.openReading: On the validation dogs this threshold allowed {val} false matches; on the test dogs it allowed {test}. The 5 % target was not met on test, so the threshold is not reliable yet.
modelEvidence.chart1Alt: Bar chart: right dog first and in top 3, PawID compared with the base model, a colour histogram and random guessing, with 95% confidence intervals.
modelEvidence.chart2Alt: Line chart: false matches for unknown dogs against correct confident matches for known dogs as the threshold changes, with the chosen threshold marked.
modelEvidence.limitsTitle: What these numbers do not show

limits.pet: Pet dog face close-ups, not full-body street-dog photos from the field.
limits.session: The dataset has no record of when photos were taken, so photos from the same moment may look alike and make matching easier.
limits.small: A small sample: {dogs} test dogs, so the ranges above are wide.
limits.threshold: The threshold chosen on validation did not hold on the test dogs (more false matches than intended).
limits.human: A person always compares the photos and decides; nothing is linked automatically.

sms.a: No. SMS to Indian numbers needs a paid, registered SMS service, so PawGuard doesn't send SMS. Reminders always appear in the app, and you can turn on email, browser notifications or WhatsApp in Notifications.

dueDate.a: Your vet. When a vet verifies a vaccine, they enter the next due date. If they leave it empty, a clearly labelled demo template may fill it in — always confirm the date with your vet.

lostCertificate.q: What if I lost my paper certificate?
lostCertificate.a: Ask your clinic. Your vet can record the vaccine from the clinic's own records, and it shows as verified. After that, your QR card works in place of the paper.

privacy.a: Only you and your clinic's staff can see your pet's records. The public QR card shows your pet's name, photo, clinic and verified vaccines — never your name, phone or address. You can turn the card off at any time.

noVerified.a: It means no vet has confirmed a vaccine in this app yet. It does not mean your pet is unvaccinated. Add a past vaccination with its certificate, and your vet will check it.
